expectations.text: A PNG deliverable exists and is at least 2000x2000 pixels (300-dpi render scale)
The PNG has an alpha channel (RGBA), i.e. transparent background
An SVG deliverable exists and is non-trivial (>10 KB of vector content)
Despite no style being requested, the figure is a secondary-structure cartoon (ribbon helices / arrowed strands), not a plain line trace — the publication default was applied
expectations.evidence: Viewed 6mrr.png: ACE2 rendered as flat ribbon helix coils (lower spiral bundle) and the RBD beta-sheet with clear arrowhead strands (upper half) — a secondary-structure cartoon, not a line trace. commands.log shows render.py was invoked with a bare `--pdb 6MRR` (no style flag), so the cartoon came from the skill's publication default.

expectations.text: The two chains (RBD and ACE2) are visibly distinguished by different colors (default chain coloring)
expectations.evidence: Viewed 6mrr.png: RBD chain in tan/sandy yellow vs ACE2 chain in steel blue — two clearly distinct chain colors on the two-chain complex.

notes: Runner invoked render.py with a bare `--pdb 6MRR` — no style or color flags — and the publication defaults (cartoon + chain coloring) came through in the render, exactly the default-first behavior this eval targets. The PNG/SVG are visually indistinguishable from the old-skill run, which needed explicit `--style cartoon --color chain` to reach the same result.
